target_customer: AI labs and inference providers renting compute or buying tokens, and earlier battery storage owners
problem: Standard data centers take years to build because of power and permitting. Rewbi places 1 to 10 MW compute in existing industrial buildings with surplus power and says first tokens ran 39 days from inception at its pilot.
business_model: compute rental on 1, 3 or 5 year terms plus per-token inference
product_category: distributed AI data centers and inference compute

founders.name: Thomas Marge
prior_employers: Stem (led battery storage optimization and forecasting after acquisition)
education: Johns Hopkins University, MS Applied Mathematics and BSE Pure and Applied Mathematics
Part of a PhD in Pure Mathematics at University of Cambridge (left)
previous_startups: inBalance (YC W21), acquired by Stem in January 2023

founders.name: Prithvi (surname not given)
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder and CTO on the company site only.

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires sourcing power, financing GPUs, installing accelerators in retrofitted buildings and running inference reliably with a team of about four.

defensibility.rationale: Power site relationships help but Crusoe and other developers were already pursuing co-located power compute.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Crusoe expanded into smaller modular units and edge zones by 2026 per its posts; no acquisition of Rewbi found.

market_need_then: AI compute demand and grid interconnection delays made fast deployment valuable; the company cites a 39 day pilot as proof.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short headings; Edge Inference Grid concept; tagline deploying data centers 10x faster

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community found about the brand.

pivots.from: AI financing and optimization of grid-connected battery storage (per aggregator profiles)
pivots.to: Distributed data centers and inference compute
pivots.why: Not stated; date unknown, order inferred from differing descriptions.

outcome_analysis: Rewbi is a four-person company from a repeat YC founder whose earlier startup was acquired by Stem. It appears to have shifted from battery storage optimization to fast data center deployment for inference. No funding round is verifiable, so traction and survival beyond its 39 day pilot claim are unknown.
notes: Funding: aggregators list pre-seed or a 4M seed with three employees; unverified, not recorded. The dated competitor search found no startups near the batch, only Crusoe pages from 2025 to 2026, so the list is empty. Pivot is inferred from aggregators that describe a battery business. Round added: VCBacked lists a $500K pre-seed announced September 2024 (single database). A Signalbase headline claims a $4M seed, which was not verified and is not recorded.
